title: EEG data offline and online during motor imagery for standing and sitting
description: EEG recordings from 32 participants performing motor imagery of sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit movements, collected in offline and online brain-computer interface (BCI) phases. Signals were recorded from 17 channels (10-20 placement) at 250 Hz while visual cues on a screen guided motor imagery and idle-state trials. Offline data were used to train machine learning models that then provided real-time task detection in the online phase.
methods_description: Participants sat in an acoustically isolated room facing a 40-inch screen about 3 m away, with a GUI guiding each trial (resting, fixation, action observation, imagining). Each session had an offline phase (six runs of 30 trials, standing or sitting) and an online phase in which models trained offline detected motor imagery vs idle state in real time. EEG was recorded from 17 channels at 250 Hz, grounded at AFz and referenced to the right mastoid.
